text:
Filip Chytil's Canucks season has been a story of getting back on the ice at all. He played just 12 games for Vancouver last season, and The Hockey Writers' headline when he returned this month read "Chytil Finally Gets a Game." He celebrated with two goals in the 6-3 win at Vegas that snapped a seven-game losing streak, then scored again the next night with a wraparound.

Since then it's been mixed. Against Chicago on Sunday he gave up the opening breakaway and took the penalty that led to the second goal, as Daniel Wagner and David Quadrelli both noted, before scoring on a bounce.

The numbers are stark in a small sample. In 13 games he has 7 points, but Vancouver takes only 30% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 with him on the ice, among the worst marks on the team, and gets bailed out by about seven goals of good luck. He's playing more than 19 minutes a night. Thirteen games is too few to judge a center, but those are minutes the Canucks need to be better with him.
